title: Are 'Buy Now, Pay Later' platforms trapping people in debt? | The Take
summary: Al Jazeera podcast interview with a Business Insider reporter surveys how BNPL works, who uses it, and the stacking and regulatory risks.

assertions.quote: As shoppers turn to the pay in four button for everything from furniture to groceries
if somebody can't pay for their grocery bill, like that's not great

verdicts.note: Plausible and consistent with survey correlations, but using BNPL for groceries doesn't by itself prove financial distress for every user.
Fed SHED: one in five BNPL users paid for groceries or food delivery, and 45% of those grocery/food-delivery BNPL users cited 'only way I could afford it' as their main reason.
LendingTree: grocery purchases made with BNPL have grown from 14% to 29% of users over two years, now the third most common BNPL purchase category.

assertions.quote: the merchant gives them a cut of the sale
people spend more money when they're using buy now, pay later
60% of buy now, pay later users say they've had multiple loans at once, sometimes three or more at the same time
Buy now, pay later companies, you guys have to follow the rules just like the credit card companies do.

verdicts.note: Pay-in-4 plans were structured to fall just below TILA's four-installment threshold; a 2024 CFPB interpretive rule extended some protections but its status is contested under the current administration.
